definitions.gloss: prime of life; vigorous middle age
definitions.explanation: The period of life when a person is at peak physical and mental vigor, roughly corresponding to the 30s through 50s. Carries a positive connotation of strength and maturity.

examples.japanese: {壮年|そうねん}の{男性|だんせい}。
{壮年期|そうねんき}に{入|はい}ってから{体力|たいりょく}の{大切|たいせつ}さを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: After entering middle age, you come to appreciate the importance of physical fitness.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{壮年|そうねん}にして{会社|かいしゃ}を{一|ひと}つの{大企業|だいきぎょう}に{育|そだ}て{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: In the prime of his life, he built the company into a large corporation.

notes:
Compound of {壮|そう} (vigorous, robust) and {年|ねん} (year, age). Unlike {中年|ちゅうねん} (middle age), which can carry a neutral or slightly negative connotation, {壮年|そうねん} emphasizes vigor and capability.

AGE STAGES IN JAPANESE:
- {青年|せいねん} — youth; young adult (roughly teens to 20s)
- {壮年|そうねん} — prime of life (roughly 30s to 50s)
- {中年|ちゅうねん} — middle age (roughly 40s to 50s; overlaps with {壮年|そうねん} but less positive)
- {老年|ろうねん} — old age (roughly 60s and beyond)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {壮年期|そうねんき} — the prime of life (as a life stage)
- {壮年|そうねん}の{男性|だんせい} — a man in his prime
- {壮年|そうねん}にして — in one's prime

REGISTER:
Somewhat formal and literary. In everyday speech, {中年|ちゅうねん} or specific age references are more common.
